sections.title: What is Kadane's Algorithm?
sections.content:
**Kadane's Algorithm** solves the Maximum Subarray problem: given an array of integers (which can be negative), find the contiguous subarray with the largest sum. The brute force is O(n²) - try every possible start and end. Kadane's does it in O(n) with a single pass and O(1) space by making one key observation: at each position, the maximum subarray ending here is either just the current element alone, or the current element extended from the maximum subarray ending at the previous position - whichever is larger.

This is essentially a 1D DP recurrence - `maxEndingHere = max(arr[i], maxEndingHere + arr[i])` - but because each state only depends on the immediately previous state, you don't need a full DP table. One variable suffices. Kadane's is the prototypical example of space-optimized DP, and understanding why the recurrence is correct (and why you reset to `arr[i]` alone when the running sum goes negative) builds the intuition for 1D DP problems in general.

The algorithm was proposed by Joseph B. Kadane in 1984 as part of a class exercise. Its simplicity is deceptive - the initialization matters (start from `arr[0]`, not 0), and the same core idea extends to much harder problems. Beyond maximum subarray sum, the pattern extends to: maximum product subarray (tracking both max and min running products due to sign flips), maximum sum circular subarray (total sum minus minimum subarray), and maximum sum rectangle in a 2D matrix (Kadane's applied row by row).

Recognizing Kadane's is important because many problems are disguised versions of it. 'Best time to buy and sell stock' is maximum subarray on a price-difference array. Any problem asking for the best contiguous window under an additive objective often reduces to Kadane's or a close variant. The algorithm is short enough to memorize completely but rich enough to anchor an entire category of array optimization problems.

sections.title: When to Use This
sections.content: Use Kadane's algorithm when the problem asks for the maximum (or minimum) sum of a contiguous subarray, or when it can be reduced to that: price differences for max profit, differences of consecutive elements, running totals. The key constraint is contiguity - if elements don't need to be adjacent, just sum all positives instead.
signals: best time to buy stock variant

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
## The Recurrence and Reset Logic

Two variables: `maxEndingHere` (best sum of subarray ending at current index) and `maxSoFar` (best sum seen across the whole scan).

At each index `i`: `maxEndingHere = Math.max(arr[i], maxEndingHere + arr[i])`. If `maxEndingHere + arr[i]` is less than `arr[i]` alone, the running sum has become a liability - drop it and start fresh from `arr[i]`. Then `maxSoFar = Math.max(maxSoFar, maxEndingHere)`.

**Initialize**: `maxEndingHere = arr[0]`, `maxSoFar = arr[0]`. Do NOT initialize to 0 - if all elements are negative, the answer is the largest (least negative) element, not 0.

## Tracking Subarray Indices

To return the actual subarray (not just the sum), track `start`, `end`, and a temporary `tempStart`. When you reset (`arr[i] > maxEndingHere + arr[i]`), update `tempStart = i`. When `maxEndingHere > maxSoFar`, update `start = tempStart` and `end = i`. At the end, `arr[start..end]` is the maximum subarray. This adds no asymptotic cost - still O(n) time, O(1) space.

## Maximum Product Subarray

Negative numbers flip signs, so the minimum product can suddenly become the maximum when multiplied by a negative. Track both `maxProd` and `minProd` at each step.

At each index: `newMax = Math.max(arr[i], maxProd * arr[i], minProd * arr[i])`, `newMin = Math.min(arr[i], maxProd * arr[i], minProd * arr[i])`. **Critical**: compute new max and min using the OLD values of both - use temp variables to hold them before overwriting, otherwise the updated maxProd contaminates the minProd calculation in the same iteration.

## Maximum Sum Circular Subarray

A circular subarray can wrap around the end. Two cases: (1) the maximum subarray does NOT wrap - standard Kadane's gives the answer; (2) it DOES wrap - the wrapped portion equals `totalSum - minSubarray` (everything NOT in the subarray, computed by running Kadane's for minimum). Answer = `Math.max(maxKadane, totalSum - minKadane)`.

**Edge case**: if all elements are negative, `minKadane === totalSum`, so `totalSum - minKadane = 0` - an invalid empty subarray result. In this case, return `maxKadane` directly.

sections.title: Core Template
sections.explanation: Single pass tracking maxEndingHere (best sum ending at current index) and maxSoFar (best overall). Resets to the current element when the running sum becomes a liability. Records start/end indices on each new maximum.

items.name: Maximum Product Subarray
items.description: Track both `maxProd` and `minProd` at each step because a negative × negative flips to maximum. Always compute new max and min from the old values of both (use temp variables) to avoid using an already-updated value in the same iteration.

items.name: Maximum Sum Circular Subarray
items.description: Two cases: non-wrapping (standard Kadane's) and wrapping (totalSum minus minimum subarray via min-Kadane). Answer is the max of both. Handle all-negative edge case by returning maxKadane when totalSum - minKadane = 0.

items.name: Maximum Sum Rectangle in 2D Matrix
items.description: Fix left and right column boundaries, compute row-prefix sums between those columns into a 1D array, then run Kadane's on that array. Repeat for all O(n²) column-pair boundaries to find the maximum-sum rectangle. Total: O(n² × m).
items.example_problem: Max Sum of Rectangle No Larger Than K

items.name: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock (Kadane Reduction)
items.description: Convert daily prices to a differences array (`diff[i] = prices[i] - prices[i-1]`), then run Kadane's for maximum subarray sum on the differences. The result equals the maximum profit from a single buy-sell transaction.
items.example_problem: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock

sections.title: Complexity
sections.explanation: A single left-to-right pass over the array with two scalar variables - O(n) time, O(1) space. No auxiliary array needed because each state depends only on the immediately previous state. The maximum product variant is also O(n) time and O(1) space for the same reason: two scalar trackers (maxProd, minProd) are maintained per step.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
items: Initializing `maxSoFar = 0` instead of `arr[0]` - when all elements are negative, the correct answer is the largest (least negative) element; zero initialization returns 0, which is wrong because no empty subarray is allowed by the problem.

Using `maxEndingHere = Math.max(0, maxEndingHere + arr[i])` - the zero-floor version only works when the problem allows the empty subarray (sum = 0); for problems requiring at least one element, this returns 0 for all-negative inputs instead of the correct least-negative element.

Maximum product variant: updating `maxProd` before computing `minProd` in the same iteration - always store old values in temp variables first; using the already-updated `maxProd` to compute the new `minProd` corrupts the minimum tracking and produces wrong answers when negative numbers are present.

Confusing Kadane's (contiguous subarray) with maximum non-contiguous subset sum - Kadane's strictly handles contiguous subarrays; for non-contiguous maximum sum (pick any subset), just sum all positive elements, which is an entirely different algorithm.

Circular variant: not handling the all-negative edge case - when all elements are negative, `minKadane === totalSum`, so `totalSum - minKadane = 0`, which is larger than any actual negative subarray sum but represents an invalid empty subarray; always return `maxKadane` directly when this occurs.

items.title: Maximum Subarray
items.why: The canonical Kadane's problem - tests the recurrence, the reset-to-current-element logic, and correct initialization to arr[0] not 0.

items.title: Maximum Product Subarray
items.why: Tests the dual-tracker variant (maxProd and minProd) and the critical requirement to update both from old values simultaneously using temp variables.

items.title: Maximum Sum Circular Subarray
items.why: Tests running two separate Kadane passes (max and min) and combining them with the totalSum formula, plus recognizing and handling the all-negative edge case.

items.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
items.why: Tests recognizing that max profit equals max subarray sum on the price-differences array - a Kadane's reduction that is not obvious from the problem statement.

sections.title: What to Learn Next
sections.why: Kadane's is the simplest DP-on-a-sequence pattern - one endpoint varies, O(n) states. Interval DP generalizes this to two-endpoint subproblems `dp[i][j]`, filled by interval length, with a split-point inner loop - the hardest standard DP category.
